entries.reason: the contract is not readable on this machine, and a row must not invent one. Neither name is declared anywhere in the 16.4 build SDK this package compiles against: 0 of its files name NSPredicateValidating and 0 name allowEvaluationWithValidator, where the same search returns 95 files for NSPredicate. That SDK is the only iPhoneOS SDK here - ~/.xmake/packages/i/iphoneos-sdk holds 16.4 and nothing else, and there is no Xcode on this machine - so no newer header can be read; and the held release ladder stops at 18.0, which is older than this pair, so the release's own metadata cannot say what either name declares either. NSPredicateValidating's required selector is the whole contract of the protocol and the method's return type is part of the method's, so writing either from the name would be a guess about a signature
entries.effect: the protocol is not declared, so a class cannot be said to conform to it and the compiler is told so; the method is not declared either, so respondsToSelector: answers NO and an unchecked call raises. Nothing in the port answers a predicate validation either: 0 of the package's 2,350 .m, .h and .c sources name either name
entries.source: the 16.4 build SDK this package compiles against, read whole - 0 of its files name NSPredicateValidating and 0 name allowEvaluationWithValidator, NSPredicate itself in 95 as the control; ~.xmake/packages/i/iphoneos-sdk holding 16.4 as the only iPhoneOS SDK on this machine; the 53 held rungs tools/cache-index/first-rung.py reads, 18.0 the newest of them
